title: Designing and printing exhaust hose mountings (wall + table) in Fusion 360, sliced in Cura, with Claude
context: This project is a personal diy project of mine. It is a part of a larger project, Basically, I am building an enclosure for my 3d printer (due to harmful fumes which are released during printing). Some parts of the enclosure I have completed, some are still remaining. For session 1, I am planning to design the exhaust hose mountings for 2 separate places. These exhaust mounts will be later 3d printed. Normally, for all my designs I’d use chatgpt to get ideas for maximizing strength in my 3d prints.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Spend more than 40 minutes making it understand the design, but after that it went smooth

Step 1.step_name: Get design inputs from Claude for both mountings
Step 1.step_action: Upload images of the wall & wood table where the mountings will be fixed, provide printer settings and material, and ask Claude to generate a basic side-view outline using "\, |, /, _" for both mountings.

nodes.label: Shares project brief and reference photos, and ask for a a stronger design with side view, top view, and front view using "\, |, /, _" which will not break easily
nodes.detail: Uploads two photos of the mounting location (black PVC board and wall with an L-clamp) plus two renders of the old failed round-collar Fusion 360 design. Describes the 4 existing leftover holes (2 on the PVC board, 2 on the wall), states the old PLA mount broke at the L-joint, and asks for a stronger PETG rebuild with the rectangular magnet slots removed.

nodes.label: Diagnoses stress riser, delivers a new design with a gusset, thickened joint, rounded corner, bossed up hole.
nodes.detail: Identifies the sharp 90-degree internal L-corner as the real failure cause (a stress riser), not the PLA material choice. Returns an ASCII side-view diagram (flange, gusset, hose passage, boss/bolt holes) per the participant's "\, |, /, _" request, plus PETG print advice: 5 perimeter walls, a modifier mesh at the gusset, 230-245C nozzle, and slower cooling.

nodes.label: Read the new design and requests exact hose-collar dimensions
nodes.detail: Clarifies the hose is a 4-inch flexible aluminum duct (similar to those used for chimneys) and asks Claude for precise collar dimensions, since "4 inch" nominal duct sizing is deceptive and doesn't map directly to a real OD.

nodes.label: Proposes collar dimensions, designs around 112mm OD, wrongly assumes hose routes through the base plate
nodes.detail: Converts the nominal 4-inch duct size to a working ~112mm OD assumption and sketches a ring/collar passage, but frames it as if the hose threads through a flat base plate rather than exiting the mount externally.

nodes.label: Corrects hose routing: exhaust exits outside the mount
nodes.detail: Pushes back with "Wait what, the exhaust goes outside the mount, right? Only then you'll be able to zip tie or but a f..." flagging that Claude's flat-plate routing assumption is wrong.

nodes.label: Acknowledges error, redesigns for external hose exit
nodes.detail: Admits error and reworks the concept. Shares a side view (90mm flange, 8mm joint tapering to 4mm, 35*30*5mm gusset, flat plate ring 10mm thick) front view (118mm ID flat plate, 10mm thick), and a spec table of ring depth 10mm, hose 118mm ID, clamp external

nodes.label: Browses old Fusion project, takes reference screenshot and sends to Claude
nodes.detail: Briefly tabs into Fusion 360 to look at the pre-existing 'Enclosure vent mountings' project (a round vent-mount model with version history from 06-2026/07-2026) to pull reference geometry, then uses a Windows Save-As dialog to rename and save a WhatsApp screenshot before uploading it to the chat.

nodes.label: Analyzes the reference screenshot and provides a new design with three views and spec table.
nodes.detail: Top view: 102mm collar, 90*90*6mm base plate. Side view: 98mm ID, 3.5mm wall, 6mm plate, 22mm from top zip-tie groove, 2mm raised retention bead, 8mm from base zip-tie groove, fillet R5mm, 30mm collar height. Front view: 102mm OD, 10mm boss O5.5mm mounting holes.

Calls this "the same mistake as before, just a different spot in the design."

Step 3.step_action: Design the table mount in Fusion 360, reusing the enclosure mount's collar/fillet spec table for a C-clamp jaw variant.

nodes.detail: Writes "ok, i have a final result now. onto the table mounting: table width is 20mm, give me something like..." closing out the wall-mount design and moving on to the second part.

nodes.label: Returns C-clamp jaw spec, reusing the enclosure table almost unchanged
nodes.detail: Returns an ASCII side-view of a C-clamp-style jaw (6mm top jaw resting on the table, 20mm gap for table thickness, 6mm bottom jaw underneath) reusing the enclosure mount's collar/fillet spec table almost verbatim -- correct on essentially the first attempt.

Sketch the table mounting jaw
nodes.detail: Sketch the table mounting jaw with 21mm width (from c2), 6mm thickness (from c2), 45mm depth and two holes for 4mm screws

Step 4.step_name: Slice 3D print files in Ultimaker Cura
Step 4.step_action: Upload the designed file in Cura, take slicer settings from Claude, and slice the design file.

nodes.label: Take screenshot of the final design and ask for 3d printing parameters for max strength
Delivers max-strength Ender 3 PETG print profile
nodes.detail: Suggests temperatures: nozzle 235-240C, bed 75-80C; Orientation: flange/wall face vertical, collar horizontal; Layer height: 0.2mm; Walls/perimeters: 5, 6 for top/bottom; Infill: 40-50% gyroid infill with a 80%-100% modifier mesh at the gusset; Speed: 35-45, first layer 20mm/s; Cooling: Fan 30-40%; Adhesion: Brim 5-8mm; Retraction:6-7mm

nodes.label: Loads STL into Cura, edit the printing parameters, and start slicing
nodes.detail: Switches to PETG, orients triangular side facing down, wall line count to 5, top/bottom layer count to 6, infill density to 40% and pattern to gyroid, printing temperature to 230C, build plate temperature to 80C, speed to 45, enable generate support, and start slicing.

nodes.label: Looks at first full slice result: 260g / 1 day 14h14m, unselects make overhang printable, and slices again
Looks at second full slice result: 258g / 1 day 15h 50m.
nodes.detail: With PETG, Standard Quality (0.16mm dynamic) and Tree support enabled, the first full slice comes back at 1 day 15 hours 50 minutes and 258g -- wildly over the participant's 100-150g / 5-8hr target, closing Step 4 as the print settings move into active tuning.

Proposes to reduce support material

Also proposes to reduce infill to 20-25%, perimeters/walls to 3, top/bottom layers to 4, layer height to 0.24-0.28mm, and speed to 50-60mm/s.

nodes.detail: Change infill density to 20, top/bottom layer count to 4, wall line count to 3, speed to 60mm/s, and start slicing again.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Took many iterations than planned, it made a few mistakes and I also had to spell out many things, For eg: Claude calculated a 120mm dia projection on a 90x90mm square base plate, which is geometrically wrong.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, but very poorly, had to spoonfeed everything in this step
